<teammate-message teammate_id="feed-empty-diagnosis" color="red" summary="FIXED #2944: app-owned projection_rev frozen at 0 froze rev-aware host caches. PR #2952">
FIXED end-to-end. PR #2952: https://github.com/pablof7z/nostr-multi-platform/pull/2952 (Closes #2944).

## Root cause (this IS the device bug, and it's NMP)
Running the real tui shell confirmed the pure-Rust stack renders (real C-ABI `nmp_app_open_feed` + `compose_chirp_runtime` + `Difference(follows,mute)` + `decode_op_feed_snapshot` all surface the notes). So the break is host-side — and I found it: BOTH the generated iOS `ProjectionCache.generated.swift:177` and the Android `ProjectionCache.kt:194` (the NMP-owned rev-aware host apply caches) skip a `Changed` row when `incomingRev <= cached.rev`. App-owned keys like `chirp.timeline.home` emit `projection_rev = 0` on EVERY tick (they're absent from the kernel's builtin rev manifest — `rung2_stamp.rs:31-33`). So the host commits the FIRST (empty) home-feed frame at rev 0, then skips every later card-bearing frame (`0 <= 0`) → frozen empty while the envelope rev (your "decodedRev") climbs to 26. That is exactly "decodedRev advanced to 26 yet no card."
 [...] <teammate-message teammate_id="projrev-fix-review" color="yellow" summary="PR #2952 verdict: APPROVE-WITH-NITS, mergeable">
VERDICT: APPROVE-WITH-NITS (doc-only nits; nothing blocking). The fix is correct, non-regressing for the emission ladder, and the emitter is the right layer. CI is fully green (all 18 checks, including file-size gate and all nextest suites). Merge it.

Findings on the six questions:

1. CORRECTNESS vs contract — SOUND. Note the ADR situation first: post-ADR-0073 reset, docs/decisions/0070-typed-read-sessions.md no longer contains any Rung/projection_rev text, and ADR-0055 no longer exists on disk; the durable rev contract now lives in the emission-ladder code itself (crates/nmp-core/src/kernel/projection_rev/mod.rs header + rung2_stamp.rs). That contract: monotonic u64 per key, advances when content changes, Rung 3 omits Unchanged. Built-ins derive rev from SourceVersions write-chokepoint counters ("option C — NOT content-hash-as-gate", mod.rs:25-37). The PR uses a content-fingerprint gate for app-owned keys — a deliberate divergence, and the right one: the kernel has zero write-chokepoint visibility into host-registered projections (opaque payload bytes from run_typed_projections, update.rs:289), so content is the only available signal. It's actually a tighter approximation of "content changed" than the built-ins' source-sum. Both mechanisms satisfy the property hosts depend on: rev never stays flat across a content change.

2. EMISSION LADDER — NO REGRESSION, strictly better. Rung 3 (kernel/update/rung3_omit.rs:63-70) decides omission from MANIFEST PRESENCE, never from entry.projection_rev; keys absent from the manifest default to Changed and are "always kept, never omitted (D3-7)". App-owned keys can never enter the manifest (build_manifest at projection_rev/mod.rs:392 enumerates exactly KERNEL_BUILTIN_PROJECTION_KEYS, test-enforced by build_manifest_covers_all_builtin_keys). So wire emission counts for app-owned keys are byte-for-byte unchanged; the only behavioral delta is host-side: unchanged payloads now keep their prior rev so rev-aware hosts correctly skip re-decode (an improvement — before the bug, they wrongly skipped everything; the naive alternative would wastefully re-decode every tick since app-owned rows are emitted every tick).

3. OTHER CONSUMERS — none affected. The only rev-GATING consumers in the tree are the generated Swift/Kotlin ProjectionCaches (nmp-codegen/src/swift_projection_cache.rs, kotlin_projection_cache) — the exact caches this fixes. The web runtime and gallery only touch projectionRev in generated FlatBuffers decode accessors (no gating). The keyed caches (refs.profile/refs.event) ride the manifest path — Tier-2, untouched. No code anywhere treats rev==0 as a sentinel (grep clean; hits are FlatBuffers defaults). projection_emission.rs's emit_rev is a separate frame-level counter, unrelated.

4. FINGERPRINT MECHANISM — sound. DefaultHasher over payload bytes is deterministic in-process; per-key (u64 rev, u64 fp) slots in a HashMap keyed by projection key — correctly scoped, no cross-key sharing (test-covered). Kernel is a single-threaded actor with &mut self, so no concurrency hazard. Monotonic for the kernel's lifetime: the tracker is created once (kernel_new.rs:235) and app_owned_revs is never reset (reset_last_emitted doesn't touch it — correct). The `rev == 0 || last_fp != fp` bump means a Changed row never carries rev 0, and A→B→A content toggles keep advancing (1,2,3). The Cleared→Changed edge is safe: Cleared rows skip the slot (keep rev 0 on the wire), and the host cache REMOVES the entry on Cleared (swift_projection_cache.rs:236-238 doc: "Cleared row → remove from cache"), so a subsequent Changed at an unchanged rev is admitted (cache[key] is nil). Epoch/session change: host caches do a mandatory reset (D4, swift_projection_cache.rs:224) while kernel revs persist — safe in both directions. Residual risks are negligible: a 64-bit hash collision between consecutive distinct payloads would delay one frame until the next change (~2^-64, same risk class as every fingerprint gate already in this file, e.g. diagnostics_payload_fingerprint); the map never prunes Cleared keys (tiny tuples, bounded by distinct feed keys opened per session — and keeping them is the monotonicity-safe choice if a host ever misses a Cleared).

5. RIGHT LAYER — yes, emitter. The generated host caches implement the documented contract correctly; the kernel was violating it. Fixing the emitter corrects iOS, Android, and any future rev-aware host at once, with no regeneration of host code needed. A host-side rev==0-always-decode guard would (a) enshrine a sentinel that's not part of the contract, (b) need duplicating in every host cache, (c) mask future emitter bugs, and (d) force re-decode of app-owned payloads on EVERY tick (they're unconditionally emitted each tick), reinstating the decode churn the rev dedup exists to prevent. No defensive host guard is warranted — decode-before-commit (D3-4) already protects against bad payloads. The one scenario the emitter fix doesn't cover is an old pinned NMP under a rev-aware host, which is just the normal re-pin flow: chirp needs a re-pin to actually get this fix on device.

6. SCOPE/FOLDING — clean. update.rs itself changed by ONE line (update.rs:396, threading &mut self.projection_rev_tracker); all new logic lives in a new dedicated module crates/nmp-core/src/kernel/projection_rev/app_owned.rs (141 lines, unit-tested) and is invoked from inside rung2_stamp::stamp_typed_projections — which is also the architecturally correct home (rev stamping is Rung 2's job), not just a file-size dodge. The test-helper call site was updated in lockstep so test and production paths stay identical. The integration regression test (nmp-testing/tests/op_feed_projection_rev.rs) asserts on real emitted frame bytes decoded exactly as a host does, and would have failed pre-fix — genuinely load-bearing.

NITS (non-blocking, one-line doc fixes):
- rung3_omit.rs:11-12 still says rung2_stamp is "a single pure function with no side-effects on kernel state" — no longer true (it now takes &mut ProjectionRevTracker). Update the sentence.
- projection_rev/mod.rs:25-28 header still declares the design is "NOT content-hash-as-gate"; the new sibling module is exactly that (justifiably, for opaque app-owned payloads). One clause scoping that statement to Tier-2 built-ins would prevent the header reading as contradicting app_owned.rs.
- Optional: a comment on app_owned_revs noting Cleared entries are deliberately never pruned (monotonicity over memory) would preempt a future "cleanup" regression.
</teammate-message>
